title: Reduce Completed pending proof render export
summary: Removed the transitional Completed pending-proof renderer flat export while preserving mediaPipelineCompletedView.renderCompletedPendingProof(). Pending Publish now refreshes Completed pending proof through the Completed namespace object, focused static/browser tests guard namespace-first access and flat-assignment regression, and generated WebView inventory/contract artifacts report 499 flat exports.
reason: Continue namespace-first WebView cleanup in the touched Completed/Pending proof domain without changing backend ownership, media policy, pending-publish drain, filesystem mutation, or source media handling.
behavior_before: completedView.js exposed renderCompletedPendingProof through mediaPipelineCompletedView and as a transitional window.renderCompletedPendingProof flat export. Pending Publish and browser proof smoke paths still read the flat alias.
behavior_after: renderCompletedPendingProof remains available through mediaPipelineCompletedView only. Pending Publish and browser smoke paths use the namespace helper, the Completed/Pending browser smoke fails if the served flat assignment returns, and the documented flat-export count is 499 across 49 files.
tests_added: Extended tests/webview/test_webview_browser_completed_pending_proof_smoke.py to use the namespace helper and reject a served window.renderCompletedPendingProof flat assignment.
Updated tests/python/desktop/test_application_facade_local_api.py to require the namespace export and reject window.renderCompletedPendingProof.
rollback_plan: Restore the window.renderCompletedPendingProof assignment in completedView.js, move the touched consumers back to the flat alias only if compatibility is intentionally required, regenerate the WebView public contract baseline and summaries, and rerun the same WebView/static validation ladder.
notes:
Source-media safety: this is a frontend compatibility-export cleanup only. It does not change backend routes, strict confirmations, repair/apply behavior, pending-publish manifests, drain behavior, filesystem mutation, source/scratch/output handling, FFmpeg arguments, or media policy. No downloads or real-media validation are required for this low-risk WebView namespace cleanup.
